verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time... waters off San Diego... Floating in the Pacific Ocean'; R4: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego... April 10, 2026'; R8: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California... April 10, 2026'.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact location, date, time, and successful splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule landed near San Diego to allow the U.S. Navy and NASA recovery teams to efficiently retrieve the crew.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'U.S.S. John P. Murtha, waiting for the astronauts'; R4: 'combined NASA and U.S. military team, will retrieve the crew... USS John P. Murtha'; R5: 'Why the Pacific off San Diego... calmer... recovery ship USS John P. Murtha'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm landing near San Diego with Navy/NASA recovery teams present, implying efficiency due to calmer waters and ship positioning, but do not explicitly state it as the primary reason.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission's landing type was Pacific Ocean splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown... Pacific Ocean'; R4: 'parachute-assisted splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R5: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean'; R8: 'Splashdown successful!'.
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources directly describe the landing as a Pacific Ocean splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission landed west of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'waters off San Diego... Pacific Ocean'; R4: 'off the coast of San Diego'; R5: 'off the coast of San Diego... Pacific Ocean'; R8: 'off the coast of San Diego, California'.
verifications.reasoning: Pacific Ocean is directly west of San Diego; sources precisely confirm 'off the coast of San Diego in the Pacific Ocean'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission completed a 10-day moon flyby mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Their journey... around the moon... 10-day mission'; R4: 'approximate 10-day mission around the Moon'; R5: 'historic 10-day mission to the moon'; R8: '10-day mission around the Moon... lunar flyby'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm ~10-day duration and moon flyby nature.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is planned to land on the surface of the Moon near the lunar South Pole.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis III will not head to the moon as previously planned. Instead, it will remain in orbit around Earth'; R2: 'Artemis III... demonstration mission in low Earth orbit'; R3: 'Crewed Earth orbital... revised to be a crewed test in Earth orbit... no lunar landing'; R7: 'possible Artemis III lunar landing sites... near the South Pole' (outdated 2022 info).
verifications.reasoning: Current sources contradict the claim, stating Artemis III is now Earth orbit only, not lunar landing; R7 is old plan overridden by later revisions.
